SRC-004: In the present paper, we take up the problem starting from appropriate Cauchy data for the Einstein vacuum equations defined on a hypersurface already within the black hole interior, representing the expected geometry just inside the event horizon.
We prove that for all such data, the maximal Cauchy evolution can be extended across a non-trivial piece of Cauchy horizon as a Lorentzian manifold with continuous metric.
In subsequent work, we will retrieve our assumptions on data assuming only that the black hole event horizon geometry suitably asymptotes to a rotating Kerr solution.

In particular, if the exterior region of the Kerr family is proven to be dynamically stable---as is widely expected---then it will follow that the C^0-inextendibility formulation of Penrose's celebrated strong cosmic censorship conjecture is in fact false.

The proof suggests, however, that the C^0-metric Cauchy horizons thus arising are generically singular in an essential way, representing so-called "weak null singularities", and thus that a revised version of strong cosmic censorship holds.
SRC-037: general vacuum initial data, with no symmetry assumed, sufficiently close to Schwarzschild data evolve to a vacuum spacetime which (i) possesses a complete future null infinity, (ii) remains close to Schwarzschild in its exterior, and (iii) asymptotes back to a member of the Schwarzschild family ... provided that the data are themselves constrained to lie on a teleologically constructed codimension-3 "submanifold" of moduli space.
SRC-040: This is the last part of our proof of the nonlinear stability of the Kerr family for small angular momentum, i.e |a|/m << 1 ... this work completes proof of the Main Theorem stated in Section 3.4 of [KS:Kerr].

answers.a_antecedent_exact: Partially. The claim's 'Cauchy data for the Einstein vacuum equations posed on a hypersurface already inside a black-hole interior' matches SRC-004's setup sentence, but the claim drops the source's load-bearing qualifier 'appropriate' and the phrase 'representing the expected geometry just inside the event horizon'. SRC-004 proves the result 'for all such data', where 'such' means the paper's appropriate interior-data class, not arbitrary data on an interior hypersurface.
answers.b_source_states_the_conditional: Yes, verbatim. SRC-004 states the conditional in the same sentence the claim condenses: 'if the exterior region of the Kerr family is proven to be dynamically stable ... then it will follow that the C^0-inextendibility formulation ... is false.' The source does not merely supply ingredients; it states the conditional explicitly.
answers.c_class_binding_supported: Not as stated. The source's data live on a hypersurface inside the black-hole interior and the passage from those data to event-horizon asymptotics is explicitly deferred ('In subsequent work, we will retrieve our assumptions on data ...'). The AF-SCC-C0-VAC-GEN class is about the maximal development of generic asymptotically flat data, so the claim needs a transfer argument that neither the claim nor SRC-004 supplies. The genericity clause of the class is likewise not established by SRC-004, whose interior-data class is a different (open) class.
answers.d_avoids_asserting_kerr_stability: Yes. The claim is explicitly conditional and the assumptions state that the antecedent is 'verified here only for Schwarzschild (preprint), polarized perturbations, and |a|/m << 1 (preprint)'. No assertion of Kerr stability was found. Two precision caveats: (i) the source says 'proven to be dynamically stable' (proof-relative modality), and (ii) the partial evidence is weaker than the assumption list suggests: SRC-037 restricts Schwarzschild data to a teleologically constructed codimension-3 submanifold of moduli space, and SRC-040 covers only |a|/m << 1.

findings.summary: Class binding to AF-SCC-C0-VAC-GEN is not supported by the cited source as stated: the theorem is about appropriate Cauchy data inside the black-hole interior, and retrieval of those assumptions from an event horizon asymptoting to Kerr is deferred to subsequent work; the class is about the maximal development of generic AF data.
findings.required_change: Either bind the claim to an interior/local class, or label it an ingredient for AF-SCC-C0-VAC-GEN with an explicit transfer obligation (retrieval of the interior data assumptions), exactly as ledger row T-301.does_not_imply already records.

findings.summary: The claim statement drops the source's qualifier 'appropriate' (and 'representing the expected geometry just inside the event horizon'), so 'for all such data' can be misread as all interior data.
findings.required_change: Restore the qualifier in the claim statement: 'for appropriate Cauchy data ... representing the expected geometry just inside the event horizon'.

findings.summary: Caveat omitted: SRC-004's final sentence records that the C0-metric Cauchy horizons are generically singular in an essential way (weak null singularities) and that a revised version of SCC holds. The claim reports only 'SCC is false' without the C0-inextendibility-only restriction.
findings.required_change: Append the restricted scope and the revised-SCC caveat to the claim, or explicitly mark the claim as covering only the C0-inextendibility formulation.

findings.summary: Antecedent modality and strength: the source says 'if ... is proven to be dynamically stable'; the claim says 'if the Kerr exterior is dynamically stable'. The assumption note cites Schwarzschild without the codimension-3 restriction and cites |a|/m << 1 without noting it is not full subextremal Kerr.
findings.required_change: Use the proof-relative phrasing and record the restrictions: SRC-037 requires data on a teleologically constructed codimension-3 submanifold; SRC-040 covers |a|/m << 1 only; full subextremal Kerr stability was not verified in the source set.

findings.summary: Scope leak in evidence_refs: SRC-035 (Hintz-Vasy, Kerr-de Sitter, Lambda > 0) is cited as evidence for the antecedent of an asymptotically flat class claim. A positive-cosmological-constant stability result cannot support AF Kerr stability.
findings.required_change: Remove SRC-035 from this claim's evidence_refs or mark it analogy-only with its Lambda > 0 scope stated.

No assertion of Kerr stability: the claim is explicitly conditional and names the antecedent as unverified for full Kerr
The first clause of the claim matches SRC-004 sentence 2 word for word
The ledger row T-301 already carries the transfer caveat and the weak-null-singularity caveat; the defect is the condensation in the claim event
review_limits: Verification is abstract-level (HTTP 200 abstract pages fetched by this reviewer); full-text page-checking of the Annals version was not performed.
I did not inspect other reviewers' work on this claim.
SRC-038 (polarized perturbations) and SRC-035 were checked for scope only.
recommended_next_falsifier: Fetch the published Annals 2025 version and locate the exact interior-data class definition; if the class is defined by conditions that are themselves retrieved from AF data in the companion paper (dynamical vacuum black holes II), the class binding in L0-16-01 may be discharged. If not, the claim must be re-bound.
